subject: science
name: Science
course: Physical Science: Classical Mechanics, Wave Energy & Matter Interactions
title: Grade 8 Science: Physical Science: Classical Mechanics, Wave Energy & Matter Interactions
overview: Grade 8 Science explores the interconnected systems of the physical, life, and Earth/space sciences using inquiry-based labs, computational modeling, and engineering design aligned with NGSS.
competencies: Formulate testable hypotheses, design empirical experiments, and interpret complex data graphs.
Construct and revise scientific models explaining matter, energy, and biological systems.
Apply mathematical relationships and physical laws to predict natural phenomena.
Evaluate technological solutions to ecological and societal challenges.

modules.title: Matter and Energy: Atomic Structure & Chemical Reactions
modules.description: Investigating atoms, molecules, the periodic table, synthetic materials, and thermal energy changes in chemical reactions.

topics.title: Atomic Theory and Molecular Models
topics.description: Modeling how atoms combine to form simple and extended crystal structures (e.g. NaCl).

topics.title: Chemical Reactions and Conservation of Matter
topics.description: Analyzing how chemical bonds break and reform to create new substances with different properties while conserving mass.

topics.title: Thermal Energy in Chemical Reactions: Exothermic vs. Endothermic
topics.description: Measuring temperature changes during chemical reactions and engineering a temperature-control device.

modules.title: Motion, Forces and Newton's Laws
modules.description: Investigating Newton's Three Laws of Motion, momentum, gravitational interactions, and electromagnetic forces.

topics.title: Newton's First and Second Laws: Inertia, Force and Acceleration
topics.description: Applying F = ma to calculate acceleration and testing bumper collision crash carts.

topics.title: Newton's Third Law and Gravitational/Electric Fields
topics.description: Analyzing action-reaction forces and mapping gravitational, electric, and magnetic force fields.

modules.title: Wave Energy: Mechanical and Electromagnetic Waves
modules.description: Modeling wave frequency, wavelength, transmission, reflection, refraction, and digitized vs. analog communication.

topics.title: Wave Properties: Frequency, Wavelength and Energy
topics.description: Modeling how wave energy is proportional to the square of its amplitude.

topics.title: Light Waves, Reflection, Refraction and Colors
topics.description: Investigating how light reflects off mirrors, bends through prisms, and absorbs into dark materials.

topics.title: Digitized Waves vs. Analog Signals in Communication
topics.description: Evaluating why digital signals (binary pulses) transmit information more reliably across long distances.
